title: runtime-fingerprint-onboarding-and-shadow-compatibility-checklist-2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This document defines the runtime fingerprinting and shadow-compatibility checklist used by Model Onboarding and the Eval team to verify that a model artifact is compatible with Redwood serving runtimes (hosted, dedicated, private) and safe to promote into production shadowing. The goal is to capture deterministic and non-deterministic runtime signals so teams can anticipate quality regressions introduced by kernels, quantization, KV cache differences, tokenizers, and batching behavior.

Motivation:

- Models with identical weights can behave materially differently under different runtime stacks (quant kernels, mixed precision, sequence-length optimizations).
- Late-stage surprises (coherence drops, hallucination shifts, functioncall decoding errors) are expensive in production.
- A standardized fingerprint and gating checklist reduces promotion risk and speeds onboarding.

Definitions:

- Runtime fingerprint: A compact set of telemetry artifacts (microbench responses, slice-anchor outputs, determinism seeds, tokenization examples, KV-cache delta signatures) that characterize how a model behaves under a given serving runtime and configuration.
- Shadow compatibility: A boolean decision to allow traffic mirroring to a candidate model in shadow mode (non-traffic-affecting) based on fingerprint proximity to the baseline and passing quality & stability gates.

Scope and applicability:

- Applies to all models entering Redwood hosted, dedicated, or private deployments.
- Required for: major model upgrades (architecture, tokenizer, quant profile), quant-shadow cohorts, and migrations between runtime families (e.g., cuBLAS->kernel-optimizer).

High-level process (1-line):

1) Generate fingerprint artifacts -> 2) Run deterministic microbench & slice probes -> 3) Compare against baseline fingerprint -> 4) Run shadow cohort with telemetry gating -> 5) Promote or rollback.

Runtime fingerprint components (required):

- Tokenization signature: token ids & byte offsets for 150 canonical prompts (see tokenization sample list below).
- Microbench harness: per-kernel per-sequence-length stepwise log-prob arrays for 12 synthetic prompts (3 seeds each).
- KV-cache delta signature: hashed set of KV-cache root-diffs captured at step 8 and step 64 for long-context models.
- Determinism seeds: deterministic log-probability vectors for 20 seed values and a variance summary.
- Functioncall trace baseline: canonical functioncall examples (3 variants per function) with expected JSON schema shapes.
- Embedding drift snapshot: average cosine to production embedding centroid for 50 anchors.

Fingerprint generation checklist (detailed steps):

1. Prepare artifact bundle:
   - Create model artifact with pinned weights + tokenizer + quant profile (if applicable).
   - Tag artifact: service_name:model_name:artifact_hash (e.g., redwood-search:reranker:v2:sha256:abcd).

2. Run tokenization signature job:
   - Command: ./tools/tokenize-signer --model-artifact <artifact_tar> --seed-corpus samples/token-sample-150.json --out token-signature.json
   - Confirm: no unknown token warnings, consistent header fields.

3. Execute microbench harness:
   - Run: redwood-eval --harness microbench --artifact <artifact> --sequence-lengths 32,128,512 --seeds 42,101,202 --output microbench.json
   - Verify: p95 step latency per token and stepwise log-probs exist for each kernel path.

4. Capture KV-cache deltas (for models with > 128 context):
   - Run an 80-step generation, sample cache dumps at step 8 & 64 using the runtime hook (see runtime-ops docs).
   - Produce hashed delta signature: sha256(kv_step8 || kv_step64).

5. Determinism sweep:
   - Run 20 fixed-seed generations and compute variance per token position. Save as determinism.json.

6. Functioncall baseline validation:
   - Execute 9 functioncall prompts. Confirm JSON schema compliance and consistent argument ordering for positional APIs.

7. Embedding centroids:
   - Compute 50-anchor embeddings, compare cosine distribution vs baseline. Save embedding-snapshot.json.

Shadow compatibility checklist (gating thresholds):

- Tokenization: 0 unknown-token warnings; average tokenization length delta <= 2 tokens for same prompt set.
- Determinism: per-token variance median <= 1e-6; max per-token variance threshold = 1e-4.
- Microbench log-prob drift: KL divergence (candidate || baseline) across microbench seeds <= 0.015.
- Embedding drift: median cosine similarity >= 0.985 to production centroid.
- Latency p95: <= 120 ms (hosted dev tier), <= 80 ms (dedicated SLO class A) for seq=128 tests.
- KV-cache delta entropy: hashed-diff Hamming distance <= 0.02 (normalized) from baseline.
- Functioncall schema match: 100% pass. Partial schema drift must have documented migration plan.

Gating policy (pass/fail rules):

1) HardReject: any Functioncall schema mismatch or unknown-token warnings -> block shadowing.
2) SoftReject: microbench KL > 0.03 or embedding median cosine < 0.97 -> require remediation and re-run.
3) ConditionalPass: minor token-length delta or marginal latency increase (<= 10% over baseline) -> allow limited shadow cohort with shortened TTL and tighter telemetry.

Shadow cohort orchestration (operational steps):

1. Create shadow cohort config (example YAML below).
2. Start redwood-shadow-runner in mirror mode for 1% of traffic, forward responses to observability sink only (no user exposure).
3. Enable additional probes: priming-cohort, cornercase-sampler, and latency-tail-capture for the candidate artifact.
4. Monitor rolling windows: 5m/30m/24h for SLI deltas and the fingerprint re-check every 30 minutes.
5. If any HardReject triggers, immediately stop mirroring and cut a rollback ticket.

Example shadow cohort config (shadow-cohort.yaml):

service: redwood-chat
model_artifact: redwood-chat:assistant-xl:sha256:ef12ab34
cohort:
  mirror_ratio: 0.01
  ttl_hours: 24
  extra_probes:
    - priming-cohort
    - latency-tail-capture
    - functioncall-monitor
  telemetry_sinks:
    - redwood-observability:eval-ingest
    - s3://prod-eval-archives/sha256/ef12ab34
gating:
  tokenization_delta_max: 2
  microbench_kl_threshold: 0.015
  embedding_cosine_min: 0.985
  p95_latency_max_ms: 120

Operational monitoring (metrics and dashboards):

- Core SLIs to visualize in the shadow dashboard:
  - eval.fingerprint.tokenization.delta (per-hour)
  - eval.fingerprint.kl_microbench (per-probe)
  - eval.embedding.cosine.median (hourly)
  - runtime.latency.p95.seq128 (5m/30m)
  - eval.functioncall.schema_fail_rate (rolling 1h)
  - eval.kvcache.hamming_norm (delta signature score)

- Alerting rules (default):
  - Severity P1: any HardReject -> Pager to ModelOnboard-1 oncall.
  - Severity P2: microbench KL > 0.03 sustained for 30m -> Slack alert to #model-onboarding and ticket auto-created.
  - Severity P3: latency p95 > SLO + 20% sustained for 1h -> email to owners.

Rollout and rollback criteria (decision table):

| Outcome | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| All gates pass | Promote to 10% live traffic after 24h | ModelOnboard Team Lead |
| ConditionalPass | Extend shadow to 48h with 0.5% mirror and run compensating probes | Eval Lead |
| SoftReject | Block promotion, open remediation ticket, require re-fingerprint after fix | Model Owner |
| HardReject | Stop mirror immediately, revert to baseline artifact, run incident review in 48h | SRE + Model Onboard |

Example CLI commands (common operations):

- Generate fingerprint: ./ci/fingerprint-run --artifact sha256:ef12ab34 --out /tmp/fingerprint_bundle.zip
- Start mirror: ./tools/redwood-shadow-runner --config shadow-cohort.yaml --start
- Run local microbench: redwood-eval --harness microbench --artifact ef12ab34 --out microbench.json
- Re-run deterministic sweep: python ./scripts/determinism_sweep.py --artifact ef12ab34 --seeds 0..19 --out det.json

Telemetry artifacts and storage policy:

- Fingerprint bundle (token_sign, microbench, kv_delta, determinism, embedding-snapshot) is stored in S3 under prod-evals/<artifact_hash>/fingerprint-YYYYMMDD.zip for 1 year.
- Short-term telemetry (5m/30m windows) retained in Prometheus for 90d; aggregated monthly rollups in BigQuery for 3 years.

Checklist to sign off onboarding (pre-shadow):

- [ ] Artifact uploaded with pinned tokenizer + quant profile hash.
- [ ] Tokenization signature generated and validated.
- [ ] Microbench harness executed for required sequence lengths and seeds.
- [ ] KV-cache deltas captured for long context models.
- [ ] Determinism sweep variance within threshold.
- [ ] Embedding snapshot compared; median cosine >= threshold.
- [ ] Functioncall baseline passed 100%.
- [ ] Shadow cohort YAML reviewed by SRE and Eval teams.
- [ ] Dashboards & alerts configured and tested in staging.
- [ ] Ownership recorded in the model registry with contact info.

Appendix: tokenization sample list (first 8 of 150):

1) "Translate to Spanish: The server returned an unexpected error code 503."
2) "Summarize the following legal clause: The purchaser warrants..."
3) "Compose a subject line for a password reset email for a fintech app."
4) "Extract dates and amounts from: Invoice #4312 dated 2025-03-01 for $4,200."
5) "Convert this markdown into JSON: - name: 'Redwood' - role: 'inference'"
6) "Functioncall test: create_event(title="Team sync", time="2026-01-15T10:00Z")"
7) "Long-context priming: [repeat a 800-token primer about prior conversation state]"
8) "Edge-case prompt: <script>alert(1)</script> What is the safe sanitized output?"

Notes and future work:

- Track a compact fingerprint vector embedding to allow fast nearest-neighbor comparisons across artifacts (outstanding infra ticket INF-2026-114).
- Add automated suggestion engine that maps fingerprint deltas to likely causes (quant kernels, tokenizer change, or decoding differences).
